# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-9 (Extended v93)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 3, harbor towns of Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford)**: Valjean and Cosette established in convent garden of le Petit-Picpus district, Paris; Valjean working as assistant gardener alongside Fauchelevent; Cosette attending as convent scholar. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound. **Winter Year 2**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak; funeral procession completed; vault burial succeeded. **Day after funeral**: Valjean and Cosette integrated into convent life. **Spring Year 3**: Currently occurring. **Recent movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead, settled in Kelmere; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures was forged. **Recent events in Staveford**: Luena Stenenridge scrubbing step; Rozek Stenenridge remarked river up in spring; letter from Rozek Stenenridge revealed mill ledger rewritten after flood (Luena burned letter); Luena argued with carter over oats price; bees hummed in lavender; frost silvered hedges; children chased hoop; rain threatened but held off. **Recent English provincial activities**: Ismira Stenson remarked salt price scandalous (Matho Stenson agreed); Ismira planned journey to Dunby before frost but roads flooded, journey postponed; Ismira spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; Ismira remarked river up again in spring (Matho noted always happens in spring); Matho read almanac aloud mispronouncing saints; someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall; baker's boy late, oven line grew long.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil; **English harbor towns**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby; numerous named individuals and activities in rural English community. Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters with yellow beams, always closed. **Chapel**: Window visible from garden; nuns perform reparation/prayer there. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Vaugirard cemetery—ancient cemetery with special Prefecture Permission for nightfall burials; Mother Crucifixion's body buried in vault beneath grand altar of convent church (concealed, no government suspicion).

**PARISIAN BANLIEUE (SUBURBS)**: Author describes philosophical study of suburb landscape—amphibious zone where trees end/roofs begin, grass/pavements, furrows/shops, divine murmur/human uproar. Extensive locations listed.

## Jean Valjean's Psychological and Spiritual Development
**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank; demonstrated gloomy talent—understood contracting to fit diameter of escape; could economize breath for hours without dying; possessed composure and coolness contagious to others.

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works in garden every day, made himself very useful; formerly pruner of trees; knows all sorts of agricultural secrets; budded ungrafted orchard trees and made them produce excellent fruit. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running and playing; distinguishes her laugh from rest.

**PSYCHOLOGICAL AND MORAL EVOLUTION**: Meditated on two places of captivity: galleys (youth)—frightful, terrible, appeared iniquity of justice; cloister (present)—chaste flame of all souls on same hearth. **CRISIS OF PRIDE**: Before convent, compared himself only to Bishop; for some time past comparing himself to men in general, and pride beginning to spring up. **VALJEAN'S REDEMPTION**: During night meditations, rose to listen to grateful song of innocent nuns weighed down with severities; blood ran cold—justly chastised raised voices only in blasphemy while he, wretch, had shaken fist at God. **WALL AS SYMBOL**: Striking realization—scaling that wall made to escape other place of expiation, now served entrance to this one. Was this symbol of his destiny?

**SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION**: In these meditations, his pride vanished. Scrutinized own heart in all manner of ways; felt his pettiness; wept many times. All that entered into life last six months led back towards Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Sometimes at eventide in twilight, knelt in middle of walk skirting chapel, before window through which gazed on night of arrival, prostrated in prayer. **CONVENT AS SANCTUARY**: Everything surrounding him—peaceful garden, fragrant flowers, children uttering joyous cries, grave and simple women, silent cloister—slowly permeated him. Soul became compounded of silence like cloister, perfume like flowers, simplicity like women, joy like children. Reflected that two houses of God received him at two critical moments: first, when all doors closed and human society rejected him; second, when human society set out in pursuit and galleys yawning. Had it not been for first, relapsed into crime; had it not been for second, into torment.

## Cosette's Integration and Development
**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Nothing trains children to silence like unhappiness. Had suffered so much, feared everything, even to speak or breathe. Hardly begun to regain confidence since with Jean Valjean.

**CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed to convent. Only regretted Catherine but dared not say so. Once said to Jean Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself Jean Valjean's daughter (natural assumption). Became convent scholar; received new garments (pupil garb).

**VALJEAN'S PRESERVATION**: Succeeded in getting nuns restore mourning suit made her put on when left Thénardiers' inn. Valjean locked up these garments plus stockings and shoes with camphor and aromatics in little valise; procured valise, set on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?"

**DAILY INTERACTION**: At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind; makes comparisons.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Current Status
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821 or earlier) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour to traverse short distances; complains of aching back as usual.

**EXECUTION OF PLANS**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket on back, left with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert. Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery with Valjean inside. At cemetery, Father Mestienne (grave-digger) dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Grave-digger lost card (cemetery entry authorization). Fauchelevent found card, buried corpse, filled grave himself; conscript wouldn't pay fifteen francs.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening work; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally and protector. Nuns do not suspect him leaves garden regularly; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit and Investigation Status
**REASSIGNMENT AND REACTIVATION**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), Javert attached to Paris police. Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence.

**REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS** (Spring Year 3): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades.

## Parisian Street Children (Gamins): Character, Nature, and Philosophical Significance
**GENERAL CHARACTER**: Gamins not devoid of literary intuition but lacking classic taste; not very academic. Being that bawls, scoffs, ridicules, fights; has rags like baby, tatters like philosopher; fishes in sewer, hunts cesspool, extracts mirth from foulness; whips up squares with wit, grins and bites, whistles and sings, shouts, shrieks; found without seeking, knows what ignorant of; Spartan to point of thieving, mad to wisdom, lyrical to filth; would crouch on Olympus yet wallows in dunghill emerging covered with stars. The gamin of Paris is Rabelais in youth. Not easily astonished or terrified; makes songs on superstitions, takes wind out of exaggerations, twits mysteries, thrusts tongue at ghosts.

**DESIRES AND ASPIRATIONS**: Two things to which he plays Tantalus, always desires without ever attaining: to overthrow the government, and to get his trousers sewed up again.

**POLICE KNOWLEDGE**: Gamin in his perfect state possesses all the policemen of Paris, can always put the name to the face of any one which he chances to meet. Studies their habits, has special notes on each one. Reads souls of police like open book. Will tell you fluently: "Such an one is a _traitor_; such another is very _malicious_; such another is _great_; such another is _ridiculous_." (All these words have particular meaning in his mouth.) One imagines he owns the Pont-Neuf, prevents people from walking on cornice outside parapet; that other has mania for pulling person's ears; etc.

**HISTORICAL EXAMPLES AND LINEAGE**: Something of that boy in Poquelin, son of fish-market; Beaumarchais had something of it. Gaminerie is shade of Gallic spirit. Mingled with good sense, sometimes adds force to latter, as alcohol does to wine. Voltaire plays the gamin. Camille Desmoulins was native of faubourgs. Championnet, who treated miracles brutally, rose from pavements of Paris; when small lad, inundated porticos of Saint-Jean de Beauvais and Saint-Étienne du Mont; addressed shrine of Sainte-Geneviève familiarly to give orders to phial of Saint Januarius.

**CHARACTER TRAITS AND TRANSFORMATION**: Gamin of Paris is respectful, ironical, and insolent. Has villainous teeth (badly fed, stomach suffers) and handsome eyes (wit). If Jehovah himself were present, would go hopping up steps of paradise on one foot. Strong on boxing. All beliefs possible to him. Plays in gutter, straightens himself up with revolt; effrontery persists even in presence of grape-shot; was scapegrace, is hero; like little Theban, shakes skin from lion; Barra the drummer-boy was gamin of Paris; shouts: "Forward!" as horse of Scripture says "Vah!"; in moment has passed from small brat to giant.

**GAMIN AS REVOLUTIONARY POTENTIAL**: All generous social irradiations spring from science, letters, arts, education. Make men, make men. Give them light that they may warm you. Sooner or later splendid question of universal education will present itself with irresistible authority of absolute truth; then those who govern under superintendence of French idea will have to make choice: children of France or gamins of Paris; flames in light or will-o'-the-wisps in gloom.

## Narrative Themes and Authorial Commentary on Paris, Audacity, and Human Progress
Author remarks burial of Mother Crucifixion under altar is perfectly venial offence—one of faults resembling duty. Notes danger of pride in comparative virtue; convent contributed completing Bishop's work in Valjean. **EXTENSIVE PHILOSOPHICAL MEDITATION ON PARIS**: Seek something that Paris has not—vat of Trophonius contains nothing not in Mesmer's tub; Ergaphilas lives again in Cagliostro; Brahmin Vâsaphantâ become incarnate in Comte de Saint-Germain; cemetery of Saint-Médard works good miracles as Mosque of Oumoumié at Damascus. Paris has Æsop-Mayeux and Canidia, Mademoiselle Lenormand. Terrified like Delphos at fulgurating realities of vision; makes tables turn as Dodona did tripods. Places grisette on throne as Rome placed courtesan; if Louis XV. worse than Claudian, Madame Dubarry better than Messalina. Paris combines unprecedented type: Grecian nudity, Hebraic ulcer, Gascon pun. Mingles Diogenes, Job, Jack-pudding; dresses spectre in old numbers of _Constitutional_; makes Chodruc Duclos. Paris drinks million litres water day but does not prevent occasionally beating general alarm and ringing tocsin.

**NO LIMIT TO PARIS**: No city has had domination which sometimes derides those whom it subjugates. Paris makes more than law, makes fashion; sets more than fashion, sets routine. May be stupid if sees fit; allows itself this luxury; then universe stupid in company with it; then Paris awakes, rubs eyes, says: "How stupid I am!" and bursts out laughing in face of human race. Strange thing that grandioseness and burlesque are amicable neighbors; majesty not thrown into disorder by parody; same mouth can blow into trump of Judgment Day, tomorrow into reed-flute. Paris has sovereign joviality; gayety of thunder and farce holds sceptre.

**AUDACITY AND REVOLUTION**: All sublime conquests are, more or less, prizes of daring. For Revolution to take place, insufficient that Montesquieu foresee it, Diderot preach it, Beaumarchais announce it, Condorcet calculate it, Arouet prepare it, Rousseau premeditate it; necessary that Danton dare it. Cry: _Audacity!_ is _Fiat lux_. Necessary for forward march of human race that proud lessons of courage permanently on heights. Daring deeds dazzle history, one of man's great sources of light. Dawn dares when rises. To attempt, brave, persist, persevere, be faithful to self, grasp fate bodily, astound catastrophe by small amount of fear it occasions, affront unjust power, insult drunken victory, hold position, stand ground—that is example nations need, light which electrifies them. Same formidable lightning proceeds from torch of Prometheus to Cambronne's short pipe.
